scenarios.title: Resident fell and is hurt, hit their head, or can't get up

triage.ask: Head strike, bleeding, new pain, can't move a limb, on blood thinners, or acting different?

caregiver: Call 911. Don't lift or move them.
Keep them warm and still. Stay with them.
Check the code status (DNR) sheet and send the face sheet with EMS.
Call the manager after 911.
manager: Call the family or guardian and the physician (CBRF: immediately).
Call the MCO care team within 24 hours for Family Care members.
If admitted or seen in the ER: file the state report (CBRF 3 working days, AFH 24 hours).
Start a fall review: footwear, lighting, meds, toileting, time of day.
owner: Confirm the state report was filed on time.
Look at fall trends across the home monthly, not blame.

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)
DHS 83.12(4)(c) (if ER treatment or hospital admission)

document: Time found, where, position, what they said
What you did and who you called, with times
Witnesses (names go in the manager-only field)

wording.casual: Found Ruth on the floor again, she probably tried to get up alone
wording.professional: At 2:40 AM, resident M-1 was found sitting on the floor beside the bed. Resident stated she was trying to reach the bathroom. 911 was called at 2:42 AM.

legal.says: States must run an HCBS incident management system by July 9, 2027. Falls with injury are a standard critical incident type.
CBRF: written report to DQA within 3 working days if ER or hospital; notify physician and legal representative immediately.
AFH: licensing agency within 24 hours if hospitalized; tell guardian and placing agency about injuries.
All member incidents to the IDT within 24 hours.
Some departments bill lift-assist calls. Ask yours (see Ask the Regulator).

clarity.q: Do I lift a resident after a fall or call 911?
clarity.a: If there is any sign of injury, a head strike, or you aren't sure: call 911 and don't lift. No Wisconsin rule says always or never lift; your written house procedure decides the no-injury case.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Resident fell, no injury, up and comfortable

triage.ask: Any pain, new confusion, or head strike in the next hours?

caregiver: Check for injury before moving.
Help up using your trained lift method or equipment.
Check on them every hour until morning.
Write it up before end of shift.
manager: Read the report first thing.
Tell the family or guardian as the plan says (CBRF: any incident, immediately).
Send to the MCO care team within 24 hours for Family Care members.
Two falls in 30 days: start a care plan review.
owner: See the monthly fall count per home.

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

notify.clock: Morning queue, unless your on-call rules say wake

document: Same as any fall: time, place, what was seen, what was done

wording.casual: Hank slid out of his chair, no big deal
wording.professional: At 7:15 PM, resident M-4 slid from his recliner to the floor. No visible injury. Resident denied pain. Assisted up with a gait belt by two staff.

legal.says: CBRF: 'an incident or injury' means notify physician and legal representative immediately, even without injury.
AFH: guardian and placing agency told of significant changes and injuries.
All incidents to the IDT within 24 hours. A message is fine when resolved with no serious harm.

clarity.q: Do I report a fall with no injury?
clarity.a: Yes, inside the home and to the care team. CBRF rules say any incident goes to the physician and representative immediately. Inclusa wants all incidents within 24 hours. DQA only needs a report if there was ER or hospital care.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Bruise, skin tear or injury nobody saw happen

caregiver: Make sure the resident is safe and comfortable.
Tell the manager today. Don't guess at causes in writing.
Describe size, color, location. Photo only if your policy allows.
manager: Start an internal investigation today: who worked, what changed, any equipment.
Use the DQA misconduct worksheet (F-00161) to decide if it must be reported.
If it can't be explained and isn't minor: report to DQA within 7 calendar days.
Keep the investigation file even if not reported (30 most recent).
owner: Make sure investigations are done without accusing anyone before facts.

notify.clock: Within 7 calendar days of knowing, if the worksheet says report
Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: Investigation steps and who was asked

wording.casual: Someone must have been rough with June, she has a bruise
wording.professional: A 3 cm purple bruise was observed on resident M-3's left forearm at 8:00 AM. Cause unknown. Resident does not recall an injury. Manager notified at 8:10 AM.

legal.says: Injury of unknown source is investigated like possible misconduct. Report to DQA within 7 calendar days unless the worksheet rules it out.
CBRF: document and report unexplained or suspicious injuries under 83.12(2).
AFH: suspected abuse or neglect goes to the licensing agency immediately.

clarity.q: Do I have to report a bruise nobody can explain?
clarity.a: Investigate first, then use the DQA worksheet. If you can't explain it and it isn't minor, it goes to DQA within 7 calendar days.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident seems sick or different (new confusion, fever, vomiting)

triage.ask: Trouble breathing, chest pain, not responding, stroke signs?

caregiver: Take vitals if trained.
Call the on-call nurse with what you see. If worse: 911.
Write down when it started.
manager: CBRF: notify the physician and legal representative immediately of a significant change.
AFH: tell the guardian and placing agency; illness over 3 days counts.
Report the change of condition to the MCO care team.
Start a service plan review if it lasts.
owner: No action unless it becomes a pattern or a hospital stay.

notify.clock: Promptly. Illness over 3 days or needing treatment counts
Change in needs: report it (Inclusa s. 7.2); incidents within 24 hours

document: Who you called and what they said

wording.casual: Walt is acting weird and super out of it
wording.professional: At 4:00 PM, resident M-2 was more confused than his usual baseline, unable to name the day. Temp 100.8 F. On-call nurse notified at 4:10 PM.

legal.says: CBRF: significant change in physical or mental condition, notify physician and legal representative immediately.
AFH: observe and document changes; tell guardian and placing agency of serious illness, illness over 3 days, or treatment needed.

clarity.q: When does a change of condition need a call?
clarity.a: CBRF: right away, to the doctor and the legal representative. AFH: promptly to the guardian and placing agency when it's serious, lasts over 3 days, or needs treatment.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident goes to the ER or is admitted to the hospital

caregiver: Send the face sheet, med list and code status with EMS.
Call the manager.
Write what happened before transport.
manager: Call family or guardian and the physician (CBRF: immediately).
Call the MCO care team within 24 hours.
If it came from an accident or injury: state report (CBRF 3 working days to DQA, AFH 24 hours to licensing agency).
Plan for return: new orders, equipment, bed hold.
owner: Track hospital transfers per month.

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)
DHS 83.12(4)(c) (only if from an incident or accident with serious injury)

wording.casual: Lois went to the hospital, couldn't breathe
wording.professional: At 6:05 AM, resident B-2 reported shortness of breath; oxygen saturation 86%. 911 called at 6:07 AM. Transported to the hospital at 6:25 AM with face sheet and medication list.

legal.says: CBRF: DQA report only when an incident or accident caused serious injury needing ER or hospital.
AFH: accident requiring hospitalization goes to the licensing agency within 24 hours.
Incidents to the IDT within 24 hours. Illness-only hospital visits are not spelled out; call anyway.

clarity.q: Is every hospital visit a state report?
clarity.a: No. The state wants accidents and injuries that needed the ER or hospital. A visit for illness alone is a family, physician and care team call, not a DQA report.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Expected death (hospice or natural causes)

caregiver: Follow the hospice plan: call hospice first if enrolled.
Don't call 911 for an expected death on hospice with a DNR, unless your hospice says to.
Call the manager.
manager: Call the guardian and family, and the people listed for emergencies.
Record date, time, circumstances and who the body was released to (AFH).
Tell the MCO care team.
Natural deaths are not reported to the state unless restraint, psychotropics, suicide or an accident was involved.
owner: Support staff. Offer time off or a debrief.

notify.who: Guardian and people in the emergency contact list
MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

notify.clock: If the death is reportable under Wis. Stat. 979.01 (for example no physician seen recently, accident, unexplained)

document: Time of death and who pronounced
Who the body was released to

wording.casual: Pearl passed peacefully overnight
wording.professional: Resident B-7 was found without respirations at 3:10 AM during a scheduled check. Hospice was notified at 3:12 AM and the hospice nurse pronounced death at 4:05 AM.

legal.says: CBRF: natural deaths are not reported to DQA.
AFH: natural deaths not reported to the licensing agency; still notify the guardian and listed persons immediately and record release of the body.
Certain deaths must be reported to the coroner or medical examiner. Check your county's office rules.

clarity.q: Do we report a natural death to the state?
clarity.a: No, unless restraint, psychotropic medication, suicide or an accident may be involved. Families and guardians are always told right away.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Unexpected death, or death after an accident, restraint, psychotropic med, or suspected suicide

caregiver: Call 911 unless a valid DNR applies. Start CPR if full code.
Don't move or clean anything if it may be an accident or suicide.
Call the manager after 911.
manager: Call law enforcement and the coroner or medical examiner as directed.
Restraint, psychotropic or suicide related: DHS form F-62470 within 24 hours of the death or learning of it.
Accident, other cause: CBRF report within 3 working days; AFH licensing agency within 24 hours (conservative reading).
Notify guardian, family and MCO.
owner: Call your insurer and, if needed, an attorney.
Arrange staff support.

notify.clock: Within 24 hours of the death or learning of it, if restraint, seclusion, psychotropic meds or suicide may be related
notify.cite: DHS death reporting page; DHS 83.12(1)(a); Wis. Stat. 50.035(5)

notify.who: DQA (CBRF, other accident or injury death)

notify.clock: Immediately for accident, suicide or unexplained death

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: Restraint, med or behavior history in the last days

wording.casual: Earl died, we think he took something
wording.professional: Resident B-5 was found unresponsive at 11:40 PM. 911 called at 11:41 PM; CPR started per full-code status. Law enforcement arrived at 11:52 PM.

legal.cite: DHS death reporting page; Wis. Stat. 50.035(5)
legal.says: Deaths related to restraint, seclusion, psychotropic medication or suicide: DHS within 24 hours.
AFH rule lists accidental death as 24-hour reportable in (e)1 and 3 days in (e)2. Use 24 hours until DQA clarifies.
Coroner or medical examiner notice for accident, suicide, unexplained deaths.

clarity.q: Which clock applies when a resident dies unexpectedly?
clarity.a: Restraint, psychotropic or suicide related: 24 hours to DHS. Other accidents: CBRF 3 working days; AFH the code conflicts, so use 24 hours.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Medication error (wrong med, dose, time, person, or missed)

triage.ask: Any breathing trouble, very drowsy, or not responding?

caregiver: Check the resident first.
Call the on-call nurse or pharmacist now. Do not guess a fix.
Record the error and omission on the med record.
Tell the manager. Facts only.
manager: Notify the physician (CBRF: immediately if it's an incident or change in condition).
Tell the guardian or representative.
Report to the MCO within 24 hours.
Review the med pass, not the person: was the system clear?
owner: Track errors as system data, not discipline counts.

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: What was given, when, by whom (manager-only field)

wording.casual: I gave Gus the wrong pills by accident, my bad
wording.professional: At 8:05 AM, resident B-9 received the 8 AM medications prepared for another resident. On-call nurse notified at 8:08 AM; instructed to monitor vitals every hour for 4 hours. Physician notified at 8:30 AM.

legal.says: AFH: record errors and omissions on the medication record. No state reporting rule for med errors found.
CBRF: an incident or change in condition means notify physician and representative immediately. No separate DQA med-error report found.
If the error leads to ER or hospital care: DQA within 3 working days.
Incident to the IDT within 24 hours.

clarity.q: Do med errors go to the state?
clarity.a: Not by themselves. Record them, call the nurse, physician and representative, and tell the MCO. If it leads to ER or hospital care, the injury report rules apply.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Resident refuses medication

caregiver: Respect the refusal. Don't hide meds in food unless ordered and consented.
Offer again later per the plan.
Record the refusal and the reason given.
manager: CBRF: repeated refusals go to the prescriber.
AFH: if a court order requires the med, notify the court and physician.
Talk with the resident about why. Update the plan.
owner: Nothing unless it becomes a pattern.

notify.clock: If the med is court-ordered and not taken

wording.casual: Pearl won't take her pills again, being stubborn
wording.professional: At 8:00 PM, resident B-7 declined her evening medications, stating she felt nauseated. Offered again at 8:45 PM; declined. Nurse notified at 9:00 PM.

legal.says: Right to refuse unless court-ordered.
CBRF prescriber notice after refusals. Cited from the earlier Rulebook, not re-read today.

clarity.q: Can I make a resident take their meds?
clarity.a: No. Adults may refuse unless a court ordered the medication. Offer, record, and tell the nurse or prescriber.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident is missing or left without anyone knowing

caregiver: Quick search: rooms, bathrooms, closets, yard, cars. 10 minutes at most.
Call the police with a description and photo.
Call the manager. Keep others supervised.
manager: Notify guardian and family.
MCO within 24 hours.
CBRF: DQA within 3 working days. AFH: licensing agency within 24 hours.
After return: health check, plan review, door and supervision review that respects rights.
owner: Review the incident without blame. Check if alarms or staffing played a role.

notify.clock: Immediately on discovering the resident is missing
Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: Last seen time and by whom

wording.casual: Earl took off again during shift change
wording.professional: At 2:50 PM, resident B-5 could not be located during a scheduled check. Last seen at 2:30 PM in the common room. Police notified at 3:02 PM.

legal.says: CBRF: law enforcement immediately; DQA within 3 working days. Exception for a competent resident who chooses not to share where they are.
AFH: licensing agency within 24 hours.
HCBS settings: freedom of movement. Door alarms or restrictions need to be in the person's plan.

legal.cite: County silver alert and police procedures
legal.says: Some counties use a missing vulnerable adult alert. Ask your sheriff.

clarity.q: How long do I search before calling police?
clarity.a: Call police as soon as you know the resident is missing. A short building and yard search is fine, but the CBRF rule says immediately.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Fire, smoke, or evacuation

caregiver: Get everyone out to the meeting place. Close doors behind you.
Call 911 from outside.
Count residents. Never go back in.
Call the manager.
manager: Arrange temporary shelter and meds.
Notify guardians, family and MCO.
CBRF: DQA within 3 working days for fire or evacuation. AFH: licensing agency within 72 hours if the fire department responded.
Fire reports also go to DQA Plan Review on form F-62500.
owner: Call insurance. Plan repairs before residents return.

notify.who: DQA (fire or catastrophe) and DQA Plan Review (form F-62500)

notify.clock: Within 72 hours if the fire department assisted

notify.who: AFH licensing agency (damage that may be a hazard)

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

wording.casual: Kitchen fire, everybody out, crazy night
wording.professional: At 6:15 PM, the kitchen smoke alarm sounded due to a stovetop fire. All 4 residents evacuated to the front yard meeting point by 6:17 PM. Fire department arrived at 6:24 PM.

legal.says: AFH: evacuation plan, semi-annual drills, 2-minute evacuation evaluation, report fire within 72 hours.
CBRF: fire, catastrophe, or evacuation to DQA within 3 working days.
Your municipality may inspect and set alarm rules.

clarity.q: How fast do we report a fire?
clarity.a: CBRF: DQA within 3 working days. AFH: licensing agency within 72 hours if the fire department came.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Power outage, no heat or water, or severe weather

triage.ask: Smoke, gas smell, or anyone unsafe from heat or cold right now?

caregiver: Check residents on oxygen or powered equipment first.
Use flashlights, not candles.
Keep residents warm or cool. Follow the building sheet.
Call the manager if not fixed in 1 hour.
manager: Call the utility. Decide on relocation if over a few hours in extreme weather.
Check refrigerated meds and food.
If residents are moved: CBRF DQA report within 3 working days; AFH damage that may be a hazard within 7 days.
owner: Approve generator, hotel or relocation costs.

notify.clock: Within 3 working days if residents were relocated
Within 7 days if damage may be a hazard

document: What was done for each resident

wording.casual: Power's out, it's freezing in here
wording.professional: Power outage began at 1:10 AM. Indoor temperature 62 F at 2:00 AM. Residents given extra blankets; resident on oxygen switched to portable tank at 1:15 AM.

legal.says: CBRF: evacuation and temporary relocation reported within 3 working days.
AFH: damage that may present a hazard reported within 7 days.
Warming and cooling centers, and medical-needs registries for oxygen users, vary by county.

clarity.q: Do we report a power outage?
clarity.a: Not by itself. It becomes a report if residents are evacuated or relocated (CBRF) or the building is damaged in a way that may be a hazard (AFH).
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Police were called to the home

caregiver: Safety first. Follow officers' directions.
Call the manager.
manager: CBRF: DQA within 3 working days if the event put residents or staff at risk.
Notify guardians of residents involved.
MCO within 24 hours if a member was involved.
owner: Review if a pattern is developing.

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: Officer name or badge and case number

wording.casual: Cops came because Roy's son was screaming at staff
wording.professional: At 5:30 PM, a visitor became verbally aggressive toward staff and refused to leave. Police were called at 5:35 PM and the visitor left with officers at 5:50 PM. No residents were harmed.

legal.says: CBRF: law enforcement called for an incident that jeopardizes resident or staff safety, DQA within 3 working days.
AFH: no separate police-call report found; report under abuse, restraint, or death rules if they apply.

clarity.q: Do we report every police visit?
clarity.a: CBRF: when the call was about something that put residents or staff at risk, yes, within 3 working days. AFH: only if another reporting rule applies.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Contagious illness or outbreak (flu, COVID, norovirus, scabies)

caregiver: Use gloves and handwashing. Keep the sick resident's items separate.
Tell the nurse and manager.
manager: Call the local health department for any outbreak.
Category I diseases: call immediately. Category II: within 72 hours.
Tell families and the MCO. Limit spread with the least restriction possible.
owner: Approve supplies and extra staffing.

notify.clock: Outbreaks and Category I: immediately by phone. Category II: within 72 hours
notify.cite: Wis. Admin. Code ch. DHS 145; P-02007

wording.casual: Half the house has the stomach bug
wording.professional: Between 11/20 and 11/22, 3 of 4 residents and 1 staff member developed vomiting and diarrhea. Local health department notified 11/22 at 9:00 AM.

legal.says: Reports go to the local (county or city) health officer.
Visitor limits during an outbreak must be time-limited and justified; HCBS rights still apply.

clarity.q: Who do we tell about an outbreak?
clarity.a: Your local health department, right away for an outbreak. They guide next steps.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident hits or hurts another resident

caregiver: Separate them calmly. Check both for injury.
Get the nurse for any injury; 911 if serious.
Write what you saw, not what you think caused it.
manager: Notify both residents' guardians (CBRF: immediately for abuse allegations).
Abuse by a resident follows elder adult at risk or adult at risk rules (s. 46.90, 55.043), not caregiver misconduct.
MCO within 24 hours for both if members.
Update both behavior support plans.
owner: Check staffing at that time of day.

notify.who: County elder adult or adult at risk agency
notify.clock: When required by s. 46.90 or 55.043 (see that scenario)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: What each person did, in order

wording.casual: Walt went off and hit Gus for no reason
wording.professional: At 5:20 PM in the dining room, resident M-2 struck resident M-4 once on the upper arm with an open hand. Staff separated the residents. No visible injury to M-4.

legal.says: CBRF: allegations against a non-caregiver or resident follow s. 46.90 and 55.043.
AFH: suspected abuse or neglect to the licensing agency immediately; crimes to law enforcement.

clarity.q: Is resident-on-resident contact abuse I must report?
clarity.a: It may be. Notify representatives and the licensing agency (AFH) right away, then follow the adult at risk rules. Don't label it in writing; describe it.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Resident is aggressive toward staff

caregiver: Step back and give space. Don't restrain.
Get help or call 911 if anyone is in danger.
Get first aid for yourself. Report your injury.
manager: Check on the staff member. Workers' comp report if hurt.
Review triggers and update the behavior plan.
Tell the representative and MCO.
owner: Make sure the injured worker is supported, not blamed.

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

notify.clock: If a worker is hurt (follow your carrier's timeline)

wording.casual: Roy punched me in the face during cares
wording.professional: At 7:45 PM during evening cares, resident C-3 struck caregiver on the left cheek with a closed fist. Caregiver stepped back and left the room. Manager notified at 7:50 PM.

legal.says: No restraint except a true emergency (see restraint scenario).
Employers must address known workplace violence hazards.

clarity.q: Can I hold a resident who is hitting me?
clarity.a: Only in an emergency to prevent injury, and it must be reported. Step away and get help first.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Staff physically held or restrained a resident in an emergency

caregiver: Use the least force for the shortest time. Release as soon as safe.
Call for emergency help if needed.
Tell the manager now.
manager: AFH: report to the licensing agency by the next business day with what happened and outcomes.
CBRF: document it in the record; DQA only if another rule applies.
Continued or planned use needs DHS approval (P-02572) and MCO review.
Check for injury to everyone.
owner: Make sure staff are trained and that a plan exists so it doesn't repeat.

notify.clock: As soon as possible during the emergency
Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

wording.casual: Had to hold Earl down, he was going nuts
wording.professional: At 9:10 PM, resident B-5 attempted to strike another resident with a chair. Two staff held his arms for approximately 30 seconds until he set the chair down. No injuries observed.

legal.says: AFH: freedom from restraint and seclusion; emergency hold only to prevent injury, report next business day.
CBRF: emergency restraint documented in the record; no DQA report unless another category applies.
MCOs report approved restrictive measures quarterly; any planned measure needs approval (P-02572).

clarity.q: When can staff restrain a resident?
clarity.a: Only in an emergency to prevent injury. AFHs report it by the next business day. Any planned restraint needs DHS approval first.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident talks about wanting to die or hurting themselves

triage.ask: Do they have a plan or the means right now, or have they hurt themselves?

caregiver: Stay with them. Listen. Don't argue or promise secrecy.
Remove obvious means if safe to do.
Call the manager now. 911 or 988 if in danger.
manager: Call the nurse or crisis line (988, or county crisis).
Tell the guardian and physician.
Plan supervision and follow-up with a mental health provider.
owner: Make sure staff have crisis training.

notify.who: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or county crisis line

notify.clock: Promptly (no hour limit in the code)

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

wording.casual: June keeps saying she wants to be dead, probably just a bad day
wording.professional: At 3:00 PM, resident M-3 stated, 'I don't want to be here anymore.' Staff stayed with resident and notified the manager at 3:05 PM.

legal.says: County crisis teams handle emergency mental health response.

clarity.q: Is a passive statement about dying an emergency?
clarity.a: Treat it seriously every time. Call the manager now; call 988 or 911 if there's a plan or means.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Someone says a caregiver abused or neglected a resident

caregiver: Make sure the resident is safe right now.
Tell the manager or designated reporter today. You may also report directly.
Don't investigate or confront the coworker.
manager: Protect residents immediately: the accused staff member is off resident contact pending review.
Notify the legal representative immediately (CBRF) and the licensing agency immediately (AFH).
Investigate and document. Use the F-00161 worksheet.
Report to DQA's Misconduct Reporting System within 7 calendar days if it meets the definitions.
Call police if a crime may have happened.
owner: Don't retaliate against reporters. Keep it confidential and factual.

notify.clock: Immediately if a crime may have occurred

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: Who reported, what they said, when

wording.casual: Sam was rough with Walt again, everyone knows it
wording.professional: At 10:00 AM, a caregiver reported observing another staff member pull resident M-2's arm firmly during a transfer at 7:30 AM. Resident has no visible injury. Staff member removed from resident care pending review.

legal.says: Protect immediately, investigate, report to DQA within 7 calendar days when required.
No retaliation against good-faith reporters; retaliation within 120 days is presumed.
Incident to the IDT within 24 hours; tell the MCO when you notify a regulator.

clarity.q: Who decides if it's reportable?
clarity.a: The facility investigates and uses the DQA worksheet. When in doubt, report. Good-faith reporters are protected.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident's money or belongings are missing

caregiver: Help look. Don't accuse anyone.
Tell the manager.
manager: Search and check records.
CBRF: notify the legal representative within 72 hours for suspected misappropriation.
If a caregiver may be involved: misconduct worksheet; DQA within 7 calendar days when required.
Police for theft.
owner: Review how resident funds and valuables are tracked.

notify.clock: Immediately if you suspect financial exploitation
Within 7 calendar days if a caregiver may be responsible

document: What is missing, value, last seen

wording.casual: Ruth's ring got stolen, probably the new girl
wording.professional: Resident M-1 reported at 9:00 AM that her gold ring was not in her jewelry box. Last seen by resident on 11/24. Room searched with resident's permission; not found.

legal.says: CBRF: misappropriation, legal representative within 72 hours.
Caregiver misappropriation is reportable misconduct.

clarity.q: Is a missing item always a report?
clarity.a: Not always. Search first. If a caregiver may have taken it, use the misconduct worksheet; theft goes to police.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Family member or visitor may be harming or exploiting a resident

caregiver: Keep the resident safe. Tell the manager today.
manager: Report to the county elder adult at risk (60+) or adult at risk agency, or law enforcement.
Tell the guardian, unless the guardian is the suspected person.
Document facts. Respect the resident's right to visitors unless there's a safety plan.
owner: Support the manager. Don't confront the family member directly.

notify.who: County elder adult at risk or adult at risk agency, or law enforcement
notify.clock: Promptly. The statute sets no hour limit; it has a 24-hour response duty on the county

notify.who: MCO care team (IDT: care manager or nurse) for Family Care members
notify.clock: Within 24 hours. Phone, not voicemail, if unresolved or serious harm
notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 7.5 (AFH and CBRF)

document: What you saw or heard, word for word

wording.casual: Pearl's son is draining her account
wording.professional: On 11/20, resident B-7 told staff her son has her debit card and she has not received her spending money for two weeks.

legal.says: Employees of DHS-licensed entities must report when the elder adult is at imminent risk and can't decide, or others are at risk. Immunity for good faith.
Each county runs intake. Put your county's number in the home's settings.

clarity.q: Where do I report abuse by a family member?
clarity.a: Your county's elder adult at risk or adult at risk agency, or the police. AFHs also tell the licensing agency immediately.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Next shift no-show or call-in, not enough staff

caregiver: Don't leave residents alone. Stay until relieved or the manager says otherwise.
Work through the call-in list.
Call the manager if not covered by the time your rules say.
manager: Fill the shift or come in.
If a resident can't self-evacuate, someone must be in the home.
Log the gap. Tell the MCO if services in a plan couldn't be given.
owner: Approve overtime or agency staff. Look at the backup plan.

notify.cite: Inclusa Scope of Service s. 6.6 (documented backup plan)

wording.casual: Jess bailed again, nobody's coming
wording.professional: Scheduled 10 PM caregiver called at 9:15 PM to report illness. Call-in list contacted 9:20 to 9:45 PM; no coverage. Manager notified at 9:50 PM.

legal.says: AFH: someone must be in the home when a resident can't self-evacuate, awake if continuous care is needed, and a substitute arranged when the licensee is gone overnight.
CBRF: enough staff on duty for the license class and residents' needs.
Adequate staffing and a documented backup plan.
Overtime pay rules apply to whoever covers.

clarity.q: Can I leave when my shift ends if no one comes?
clarity.a: Not if residents would be alone. Call the manager; staying until relieved protects residents and you.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Staff member seems impaired, or a worker is charged with a crime

caregiver: If a coworker seems impaired, keep residents safe and call the manager now.
Don't confront them alone.
manager: Remove from resident care. Arrange a safe ride home.
A pending charge or conviction that relates to care: AFH licensing agency within 48 hours; DQA by the next business day.
Recheck the background (caregiver law).
owner: Follow your HR policy. Talk to an employment lawyer before discipline.

notify.clock: Within 48 hours of a pending charge or conviction (licensee or service provider)
By the next business day after learning of a charge

document: What you saw (smell, speech, balance), not labels

wording.casual: Mike was totally drunk on shift
wording.professional: At 11:30 PM, staff member was observed with slurred speech and unsteady walking. Removed from resident care at 11:35 PM; manager arrived 12:05 AM.

legal.says: Caregiver background law: report charges by the next business day.
AFH: crime substantially related to care, licensing agency within 48 hours.

clarity.q: A caregiver told me they were arrested. Now what?
clarity.a: If it could relate to caregiving, report: AFH licensing agency within 48 hours, DQA by the next business day. Keep them off resident care until it's sorted.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Resident refuses care (shower, cares, appointments)

caregiver: Respect the no. Offer again later or with another caregiver.
Never force or threaten.
Log each refusal and what was offered.
manager: Look for the reason: pain, fear, timing, privacy.
Update the plan with the resident and guardian.
If health is at risk: involve the nurse and physician.
owner: None unless it repeats across homes.

notify.clock: When refusals put health at risk

wording.casual: Hank refused his shower again, being difficult
wording.professional: Resident M-4 declined his scheduled 9 AM shower, stating he prefers afternoons. Offered a sponge bath; declined. Re-offered at 2 PM; accepted.

legal.says: Self-direction and treatment choice.
HCBS settings: autonomy and choice in daily activities.

clarity.q: Is it neglect if I don't make them shower?
clarity.a: No, if you offer, document, and work the plan. Neglect is failing to provide care, not respecting an informed no.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Guardian and resident disagree (or family members disagree)

caregiver: Stay neutral. Don't take sides or pass messages.
Refer decisions to the manager.
manager: Check what the guardianship covers (person, estate, limited).
Follow the guardian's legal decisions, but tell the guardian the resident's wishes.
Offer the ombudsman (60+) or Disability Rights Wisconsin (under 60).
If you think the guardian isn't acting in the person's interest, call the county.
owner: Stay out of family politics. Back the manager.

notify.clock: If a guardian may be harming the resident

document: Each person's wishes, in their words
What decision was made and by whom

wording.casual: Mom wants out but the daughter says no way
wording.professional: Resident C-1 stated she would like to visit her sister for the weekend. Guardian stated by phone at 2:00 PM that the visit is not approved at this time. Resident informed; ombudsman contact offered.

legal.says: Presumed competent unless adjudicated; if a guardian places someone who objects, notify the county ch. 55 agency.
Guardianship scope set by the court order.

clarity.q: Who decides: the guardian or the resident?
clarity.a: The guardian, for decisions the court gave them. The resident still has rights and a voice. Offer the ombudsman when they disagree.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Family member complains about care

caregiver: Listen. Thank them. Don't argue or explain away.
Share only what the release list allows.
Write the complaint down and give it to the manager.
manager: Call back within one business day (house goal).
Follow the written grievance procedure. Give a written summary of findings and actions.
Inclusa members: formal complaints to the IDT within 48 hours.
Remind them of the ombudsman and licensing agency. No retaliation.
owner: See complaints by theme monthly.

notify.clock: Formal complaints within 48 hours of receipt

document: Written summary to the resident or guardian (AFH)

wording.casual: Roy's daughter is mad again about laundry
wording.professional: On 11/25 at 4:00 PM, a family member reported that resident C-3's clothing was returned to the wrong room twice this week. Manager to follow up by 11/26.

legal.says: AFH: grievance procedure, written summary, access to advocates, no retaliation.
CBRF: written grievance procedure.
Formal complaints to the IDT within 48 hours.

clarity.q: Do we have to tell the MCO about a family complaint?
clarity.a: For Inclusa members, a formal complaint goes to the care team within 48 hours. Check other MCOs' rules.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Home wants to end a resident's stay (discharge)

manager: Check the service agreement's discharge terms.
Give 30 days' written notice to resident, guardian, service coordinator, placing agency and representative.
Help find a new place. Only skip the 30 days for an emergency to prevent harm.
owner: Approve the decision. Get legal advice if it's contested.
caregiver: Keep care the same during the notice period.

notify.who: Resident, guardian, service coordinator, placing agency, representative

notify.clock: Right away so they can find a new provider

wording.casual: We can't handle Earl anymore
wording.professional: The home is giving written 30-day notice of termination of services, effective 12/27, because resident B-5's assessed needs exceed the care the facility is licensed to provide.

legal.says: AFH: 30 days' written notice, except emergency termination to prevent harm.
CBRF: 30-day notice and listed reasons.

clarity.q: How much notice do we give to discharge?
clarity.a: 30 days in writing, to everyone listed. Emergencies to prevent harm are the only exception.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: A state surveyor shows up (unannounced)

caregiver: Be polite. Ask for ID. Call the manager.
Answer honestly. It's okay to say 'I'd check our procedure.'
Keep caring for residents.
manager: Come in or join by phone. Give requested records promptly.
Inclusa members: send survey results and any plan of correction to Inclusa within 2 days after the visit.
Plan of correction by the deadline on the statement of deficiencies.
owner: Review the statement of deficiencies and fund fixes.

notify.clock: Within 2 days after the visit ends, with any plan of correction

wording.casual: State lady is here digging through everything
wording.professional: DQA surveyor arrived at 9:00 AM for an unannounced visit. Manager arrived at 9:20 AM. Requested records provided by 10:00 AM.

legal.says: Comply with department and licensing agency information requests.
Regulatory visit results to Inclusa within 2 days.

clarity.q: Do I have to let a surveyor in without the manager?
clarity.a: Yes. Be polite, check ID, call the manager, and keep caring for residents.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Care manager (MCO) asks for records, changes, or something that conflicts with the rule

caregiver: Refer requests to the manager unless it's routine and in the plan.
manager: Log the request with date, who, and what. Ask for it in writing.
Share records only as allowed. MCO care team is part of the member's care.
If the request conflicts with DHS 83/88, follow the licensing rule and ask the MCO to put it in writing; use Ask the Regulator.
owner: Watch request volume and time cost per MCO.

document: Request log: date, who, what, response, proof of delivery

wording.casual: Care manager wants all of June's notes by tomorrow, again
wording.professional: On 11/25, the care manager requested resident M-3's last 30 days of progress notes by 11/26. Request logged; records sent via secure email 11/26 at 10:00 AM.

legal.says: Report changes in needs and needed service changes.
Record confidentiality and release rules still apply.

clarity.q: MCO rule or state rule: which wins?
clarity.a: The licensing rule is the floor. An MCO can ask for more, not less. When they conflict, follow the stricter one and get it in writing.
clarity.label: reading

scenarios.title: Ombudsman visits or a resident asks for an advocate

caregiver: Welcome them. Residents can talk privately with the ombudsman.
manager: Don't ask the resident what they said.
Work with the ombudsman on solutions. No retaliation.
owner: Ask the ombudsman program for free staff training on rights.

wording.casual: Ombudsman came, someone must have complained
wording.professional: Regional ombudsman visited on 11/25 from 1:00 to 2:00 PM and met with residents.

legal.says: Residents have access to advocates including the ombudsman.

clarity.q: Do we have to let the ombudsman talk to residents alone?
clarity.a: Yes. It's a resident right, and the program also offers free rights training for staff.
clarity.label: rule

scenarios.title: Someone asks for a resident's information (family, phone call, records)

caregiver: Share only what the release list allows. 'I'll have the manager call you back' is always fine.
Never post or text resident details on personal phones.
manager: Check the release and who is the legal representative.
Copies to resident, guardian or representative as soon as practicable once authorized in writing (AFH).
owner: Confirm whether the home is a HIPAA covered entity (it bills electronically?) and train accordingly.

document: What was released, to whom, authorization on file

wording.casual: Gus's niece called asking about his meds
wording.professional: A caller identifying as resident B-9's niece requested medication information at 3:00 PM. Not on the release list; caller referred to the manager.

legal.says: Applies if the home is a covered entity.
Health record confidentiality and resident right to records.

clarity.q: What can I tell a family member on the phone?
clarity.a: Only what the release list allows. When unsure, take a message for the manager.
clarity.label: rule
